subject: biology
title: Plant Biology (HL) Adventure 1: Xylem, transpiration and cohesion-tension
welcome_lead: Today you'll pull water up a 100 m redwood with sunlight.
meta_desc: Biology HL — xylem, transpiration, cohesion-tension theory, stomata, abiotic factors.
final_note: You learned xylem is dead lignified vessels, transpiration pulls water up by cohesion-tension, and stomata balance gas exchange with water loss.

concepts.def: Water loss by evaporation from leaves
Water column pulled up by H-bonds

walkthroughs.body_html:
Root hair cells extend SA. Water enters by osmosis down water potential.

Two pathways across cortex:
- Apoplast — through cell walls.
- Symplast — through plasmodesmata.

At the endodermis, the Casparian strip (waterproof suberin) forces apoplastic water into symplast — controls entry to xylem.

Xylem vessels are dead, hollow, lignified tubes — minimal resistance.

Cohesion-tension theory: water evaporates from mesophyll → tension drawn through xylem all the way to roots. Water's cohesion (H-bonds) holds the column together; adhesion to xylem walls helps.

Pulled to 100 m+ in Sequoia.

Guard cells flank each stoma. K⁺ uptake → water in → guard cells turgid + curved → stoma opens.

Open = CO₂ in for photosynthesis, but H₂O out.

Abiotic factors raise transpiration: high light, low humidity, warm temperature, wind. Xerophytes (cacti) adapt with sunken stomata, thick cuticle, CAM photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: What does negative feedback do in homeostasis?
options: Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
It reverses a change in a controlled variable, bringing it back towards the set point.
Negative feedback makes a process get worse or amplifies the change.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9?
options: It directs Cas9 to the specific DNA sequence to cut by base-pairing with the target.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
Guide RNA is the new sequence that gets inserted into the genome.

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.
From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.
